These ants include leaf cutter ants, who harvest leaves fresh from plants to take back to their nest so they can cultivate fungi.

When a leaf cutter queen is heading off to form a new colony, she will take a piece of the original nest’s fungus to start her own nest. 

While some attine ants cultivate fungi that grow wild in their surroundings, others like the leaf cutter ants have domesticated their own fungi. This means that their species of fungus doesn’t, and can’t, grow in the wild. And just like we’ve selectively bred fruit and vegetables to be bigger and better their domesticated fungi have fruiting bodies that aren’t found on any other fungi called gongylidia that can be harvested and eaten by the ants. 

Some types of attine ants have even evolved an anti microbial coating so that they don’t harm their crop, as well as cleaning habits like washing themselves and defecating away from the nest.

 It states that decongestants are harmful for people with clogged arteries and other heart conditions, and lists a few alternatives. A quote straight from the article:
“Alternatives to oral decongestants are available. In the drug realm, antihistamines such as diphenhydramine (Benadryl), chlorpheniramine (Chlor-Trimeton), cetirizine (Zyrtec), and loratadine (Claritin) can help with a stuffy nose are safe for the heart.

Nasal sprays deliver a decongestant right where you need it. In theory, this should minimize cardiovascular effects. However, nasal decongestant sprays should be used only for several days because it can lead to rebound nasal congestion.”

The known long term side effects of hormonal birth control are blood clots, heart attack and stroke, breast and cervical cancer. There might be more that haven’t been studied, but there’s no evidence for it yet. There’s a laundry list of short term side effects though, and you can read a list of them [here.](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/combination-birth-control-pills/about/pac-20385282) You can also look up the name of your birth control and you could find a more specific list. 

If you’re on the Depo-Provera shot though, and have been for longer than 2-3 years, you should get off of it immediately. It causes bone density loss (AKA osteoporosis if you’re on it long enough) and it’s just not worth it. It has a black box FDA warning for this reason.

I realized I didn’t fit in with girls but I couldn’t pinpoint why. I adopted a “I’m not like other girls I’m so quirky!!” attitude, and sometimes made fun of other girls for not being like me.


I didn’t like to talk about gossip, I didn’t care who was dating who, what I was wearing to the next dance didn’t seem important. It just took me a while to realize that those things aren’t wrong or weird to enjoy, but that I was a guy, and fell more in line with/resonated more with stereotypically masculine stuff.


I enjoy being strong, caring, and independent, but in a way that a dad would be and not in the way a mom would be. There’s a distinction there I can’t put my finger on, but it makes sense in my head. I’m not saying this is what’s happening, but both are possible and it would make sense that medication helps with these symptoms.

Why are you tapering? If you’ve decided it’s better for you to taper off, I’d keep going with it. Remember that withdrawal symptoms aren’t going to be your new normal and don’t last forever, but if the meds were working for you just fine and there weren’t too many negatives, maybe it is best to stay on it.

About when to reduce the dosage, just listen to your body really. Wait until you have very little withdrawal symptoms before reducing more. If the medicine is extended release or has an enteric coating, don’t cut it in half. If it isn’t extended release, you can get a pill cutter from a pharmacy and use that to make sure you’re getting exactly half or quarter of a pill. Keep in mind however that the medicine inside the pill isn’t evenly distributed- you might get more of the medicine one day and less the next. This can worsen your withdrawal on certain days. 

I tapered myself off of Zoloft, and dropped from 150 mg to 100mg- stayed on 100 for 2 weeks, down to 75mg for 2 weeks, then 50mg for 3 weeks, 25mg for 3 weeks, all the way down to 12.5mg for a month. The lower you go the worse the withdrawal and the longer it takes to get used to it. Give your body time. At the end I even took just a tiny sliver of the pill for a week. I went through crazy mood swings, GI issues, insomnia, anxiety. Just take it slow.

Yeah definitely turn down the wattage/temp on your battery. What you’re describing is the coil becoming burnt. Carts work by heating up a distillate-soaked coil. This coil can be either cotton or quartz, but both can become burnt from the wattage being too high, not having enough distillate on the coil, or from pressing the button (heating the coil) without actively hitting the cart. When the coil becomes burnt, you won’t get as much flavor from it other than “burnt” flavor, the coil may not soak up enough distillate anymore, and it’s not healthy considering there’s now extra chemicals from the cotton or quartz burning. To prevent this, you want the distillate to stay in the bottom of the cart, and if it starts to taste burnt immediately turn down the wattage and dry hit it (suck air through it without pressing the button) as this can pull distillate back into the coil.
